chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-A'ala ibn Fuzayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Magnify your companions and revere them, and let not some of you scowl at others, nor harm one another, nor envy one another. And beware of stinginess; be the sincere worshippers of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical behaviors Muslims should exhibit towards their companions according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the spiritual etiquette (*adab*) within the Shia community by linking social harmony to spiritual purity. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that avoiding internal discord—such as scowling, harm, and envy—is essential to becoming *'ibad Allah al-mukhlasin* (sincere worshippers), a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the rights of the believer over his brother.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al A’ala Bin Fuzayl,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Magnify your companions and revere them, and neither should some of your scowl at the others, nor harm, nor envy (each other). And beware of the stinginess! Become sincere worshippers of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-‘Ala’ ibn Fudayl from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far (a.s.) would say, ‘Dignify your people, honor them and do not be aggressive toward each other, do not harm each other and do not be jealous of each other. You must never be miserly and always be sincere servants of Allah.’”
